why.title: You Pump. They Collect. (Stickman Psychology Animated Short)
why.why: It uses minimal stickman animation to deliver an aggressive, high-breakout visual metaphor about systemic exploitation, triggering immediate outrage and curiosity.

why.title: Nobody Is Coming. Get Up. 💀
why.why: A brutally blunt, tough-love hook paired with extreme sub-to-view ratios proves viewers are deeply hooked by dark, confronting self-reliance truths.

why.title: The Genius Rats Experiment
why.why: Framing historical or psychological studies as bizarre animated experiments taps into fast-paced narrative storytelling that demands visual resolution.

why.title: Why the Second Draw Always Wins
why.why: It leverages counter-intuitive game theory with a curiosity-gap title that makes the viewer feel like they are learning an unfair life hack.

hook_patterns: A harsh, unvarnished truth delivered in the first 2 seconds alongside a absurd visual metaphor
Counter-intuitive game theory or rules presented as secret life hacks you're currently losing
Animated narrative reinactments of famous dark or bizarre psychological experiments
todays_angle: Translate dark, high-breakout psychological principles into comedic, passive-aggressive banter between Leo and Mia.
ideas: Leo tries to use the 'Spotlight Effect' to explain why he can't leave the house with a tiny smudge on his shirt, while Mia proves nobody even noticed he wasn't wearing shoes.
Mia uses 'Learned Helplessness' to justify why she won't reach for the TV remote across the couch, staging a full tragic experiment with Leo as the evaluator.
Leo realizes he's a victim of the 'Decoy Effect' at a coffee shop and tries to stage an intervention for Mia, only to fall for the exact same trick 5 seconds later.
avoid: Generic 'Money can't buy love' romance advice audio over static slides
Overdone gross-out physical humor like pull-my-finger tropes without a brainy twist
